Read gaze and pupil data

Source: R/read.R
read_g3_gaze.Rd

Parses gazedata.gz into one row per sample. Samples where the glasses detected no gaze are kept, with NA values, so that the time series stays complete. Lines that cannot be parsed, such as the cut-off last line of an incomplete file, are skipped with a warning; see g3_fill_gaps() to replace them with empty rows. A file whose compressed data are damaged cannot be read and gives an error.

Usage

read_g3_gaze(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a recording folder or directly to a gazedata.gz file. Several paths, or the output of list_g3_recordings(), read several recordings into one tibble.

Value

A tibble with columns:

recording

Name of the recording folder. If two recordings in path have folders of the same name, the full path is used instead.

time

Seconds since the start of the recording.

gaze2d_x, gaze2d_y

Gaze point in normalised scene camera coordinates, with (0, 0) at the top left of the video frame and (1, 1) at the bottom right.

gaze3d_x, gaze3d_y, gaze3d_z

Point where the gaze of the two eyes meets, in millimetres from the scene camera.

left_origin_x, ..., right_direction_z

Position of each eye in millimetres from the scene camera, and its gaze direction as a unit vector.

left_pupil, right_pupil

Pupil diameter for each eye in millimetres, the unit given in the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 Developer Guide.

valid_left, valid_right

Whether the glasses reported data for that eye.

valid

Whether the sample has a gaze point. The glasses can estimate one from a single eye, so this can be TRUE when one eye is invalid.

See the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 Developer Guide for the coordinate systems.

The glasses record gaze at 50 or 100 Hz, in the same file format. The rate is not stored in the recording, so functions that need it work it out from the timestamps.

Examples

gaze <- read_g3_gaze(g3_example())
gaze
#> # A tibble: 1,497 × 24
#>    recording   time gaze2d_x gaze2d_y gaze3d_x gaze3d_y gaze3d_z left_origin_x
#>    <chr>      <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 recording 0.0180    0.460    0.842     49.0    -208.     549.          32.1
#>  2 recording 0.0381    0.457    0.846     58.0    -237.     616.          32.1
#>  3 recording 0.0581    0.455    0.850     70.7    -279.     718.          32.1
#>  4 recording 0.0782    0.445    0.873     84.7    -295.     710.          NA  
#>  5 recording 0.0982    0.444    0.876     86.0    -298.     709.          NA  
#>  6 recording 0.118     0.445    0.869     89.4    -306.     745.          32.1
#>  7 recording 0.138     0.446    0.869    132.     -466.    1134.          32.1
#>  8 recording 0.158     0.449    0.867    230.     -849.    2079.          32.1
#>  9 recording 0.178     0.451    0.867    272.    -1046.    2559.          32.1
#> 10 recording 0.198     0.453    0.866    427.    -1686.    4131.          32.1
#> # ℹ 1,487 more rows
#> # ℹ 16 more variables: left_origin_y <dbl>, left_origin_z <dbl>,
#> #   left_direction_x <dbl>, left_direction_y <dbl>, left_direction_z <dbl>,
#> #   left_pupil <dbl>, right_origin_x <dbl>, right_origin_y <dbl>,
#> #   right_origin_z <dbl>, right_direction_x <dbl>, right_direction_y <dbl>,
#> #   right_direction_z <dbl>, right_pupil <dbl>, valid_left <lgl>,
#> #   valid_right <lgl>, valid <lgl>

recordings <- list_g3_recordings(dirname(g3_example()))
read_g3_gaze(recordings)
